prediction.likelyOutcome: Montgomery Park is more likely than not to prevail on its position that NCO's early termination was ineffective and that rent remained due, given its contemporaneous notice disputing satisfaction of the termination conditions, but this is a genuine, fully-contested bench-trial issue rather than a sure thing. The quantifiable recovery on this record centers on the $313,662.76 demanded in the July 2011 default letter, likely augmented by contractual attorney's fees and default-rate interest in an amount not yet ascertainable from the materials, with a potentially much larger unquantified additional rent claim if the lease is found to have remained in force through the balance of its term.

outcome.description: After a bench trial the district court entered judgment for Montgomery Park on its past-due-rent counterclaim of $9,854,566.95 plus postjudgment interest (upheld in earlier Fourth Circuit appeals at 842 F.3d 816, 918 F.3d 388 and 40 F.4th 123). The court then awarded $2,074,379.88 in attorneys' fees and nontaxable expenses, $115,942.10 taxable costs and $1,576,036.07 default interest ($3,766,358.05 total). In this fifth appeal the Fourth Circuit affirmed the fee/cost award (including expert fees) but vacated the default-interest component, holding interest runs only from the August 24, 2022 demand, and remanded for recalculation; the underlying rent judgment was not disturbed.
